Hello.description:
The first line a client sends.

A listener reads `protocol` leniently first, through a struct with only that field, so a
newer client that sends a claim it does not know still gets `Refused { Version }`. A
client never acts on a `Refused` that came before the core's proof beyond showing it:
anyone on the socket can send one.

auth.description: Which secret the client holds; absent in-process, required on every transport.

client.description:
Who is asking, such as `tui`; threads it creates carry it as their source. 1 to 40
of `[A-Za-z0-9 ._-]`.

nonce.description: 32 random bytes, lowercase hex; empty in-process.

Proof.description: The client's second line: its own proof, and what it wants.

Greeting.description: Every line the core sends during the handshake.

oneOf.description: The answer to a `Hello` that can go on: the core proves it holds the secret.

RequestFrame.description: What the remote client sends: a request and the number its response comes back under.

ServerFrame.description: What the core sends: answers, and what it pushes on its own.

oneOf.description: The status as it is now, first on a new stream and after each change.

Activity.description: What the thread's tools did, from every call it made.

AgentNode.description: One agent in the tree a client draws: the chat at the root, then whom each may ask.

enabled.description: Its own switch; the chat is always on.

links.description: The agents it may ask, drawn under it or elsewhere in the tree.

version.description: `None` for the chat and the built-in general agent, which have no AGENT.md.

problems.description: Agents that could not be read.

skipped.description: Links to agents that are not there; skipped, the rest works.

oneOf.description: The archive contains config secrets as well as chat history.
Every configured provider, checked just now, and the model in use.
Every thread talks to this model from now on.
The client closes the open thread and shows an empty one.
The same, and the thread it starts is a temporary one.
The user's messages the thread can go back to, oldest first.
The effort now; `changed` when the command set it.
The thread's background jobs, oldest first.
The thread's sources, oldest first.

ApprovalPolicy.description:
Ask is the default. Sandbox runs commands without asking, confined by the system to
the working folders; paths outside them and the screen are still asked. Full access
answers every request with yes. Arbiter hands each request to an agent that decides
in the user's place. The config folder stays closed either way.

ApprovalRequest.description: A request as the client sees it; `id` is what its answer names.

session.description:
What a yes for the session covers, as the core decides it: the folder of the
path, or the program of a plain command. `None` when it cannot be offered.

steps.description:
Every step of a batch of screen actions, or every gate command of a plan, in
order; empty for a single request.
The user answers for all of them, so a client shows each one, never a summary.

ApprovalStep.description: One step of a batch as the user sees it before saying yes.

allowed.description: A session grant covers it already; it is listed so the user sees the whole batch.

number.description: Its place in the batch, from 1.

request.description: What the step would ask alone: its kind and what it does.

Arbiter.description:
The arbiter's settings. The prompt only guides its judgment: the core still asks the
user when the answer is unclear and never lets it allow what the approval mode forbids.

prompt.description: The user's review prompt; `None` keeps the built-in one.

Balance.description: Money left on a provider account, as the provider wrote it.

left.description: A decimal number; none when the key has no spending limit.

Busy.description: How much the core is doing, so a client can tell whether a restart would hurt.

CallHealth.description: Whether a provider's calls are answered. Times are Unix milliseconds.

oneOf.description: Its newest call was answered, and every one since `since`.

Its calls fail with `kind`, the first of them at `since`; `last_answered` is when
one was answered before, if any was since the core started.

Card.description:
A durable card reference, carried separately from model-visible text. IDs are generated
locally; neither a URL nor a caller-supplied path is used as a storage filename.

duration_ms.description: How long a sound plays, in milliseconds; zero when unknown, and for pictures.

for_model.description:
The model sees it with the tool result that made it, such as a screenshot; other
cards are for the user only.

kind.description: What the card holds. Records written before sounds existed read as pictures.

CatalogRequest.description: The files the user edits through the settings, and the MCP servers.

oneOf.description:
The skill packs with their skills and switches; answered with
`Response::SkillPacks`.
Answers with the name it was saved under, or none when the text removed it.
Answers with the page that signs in.
Empty text removes the snippet.
Which secrets are set, without their values.
The speech servers that are set up.

staged.description: Whether the index holds a change of it, all or part.

ChangeSum.description: What the thread changed in its project, from the change ledger.

added.description: Lines, from the diffs that were kept.

ChatGpt.description: The sign-in with a ChatGPT account, which connects OpenAI without an API key.

oneOf.description: The browser has the sign-in page; the core waits for it to come back.

account.description: The account's email, or a plain name when it gave none.

oneOf.description: The last sign-in did not complete, and why.

Check.description: One check of a pull request; text plain and capped by the core.

url.description: Its page, https only; empty when GitHub gave none that is safe.

workflow.description: The workflow it runs in; empty when GitHub names none.

CheckFailure.description: What kind of failure a provider check met, so a client can say it plainly.

oneOf.description: No connection, or no answer in time.
HTTP 401 or 403: the key was refused.
An answer, but not a model list of the OpenAI API.

CheckStage.description: Where one check stands, finer than `CheckState`.

CheckState.description: How a pull request's checks, or one check, stand.

Checks.description:
A pull request's checks counted. `state` is the worst of them: failing over
running over passing; `None` when there are none.

list.description:
The checks themselves: failed first, then running, queued, passed and skipped;
capped, so `total` may count more.

Children.description: The processes below the app's own, summed.

Claim.description: Which secret a client says it holds.

oneOf.description: The core's own key, for the user's own apps.
A token the user made, named by its id.
The desktop window.
The terminal.
The browser.

Clock.description: A time of day on this machine's clock.

oneOf.description: Writes a portable archive of config and chat data; never sends it anywhere.
Summarizes the context so far; the argument is extra instructions for the summary.
Lists the threads to open again; a client fills in the folder it runs in.
Leaves the open thread for a new one, created with its first message.
The same, for a chat kept in memory only and gone when the core stops.
Lists the providers with their models, or switches to `provider/model`.

Answers `Providers` with the enabled providers at once, none of them asked yet
(`name` none), or with the one provider checked; a client asks each on its own to
show them as they answer.
What a client offers to switch: tools, skills, agents and limits.
What the next request of the thread carries; a client fills in its open thread.

Describes the thread in detail and goes on in a new thread from that; the
argument is extra instructions for the description.
The newest version on the update channel; `dev` or `stable` switches it first.
Shows the reasoning effort, or sets it to a supported level or default.
Creates a draft goal; shows, approves, confirms, pauses, resumes or clears it.

Lists the user's messages of a thread; a client fills in its open thread. With a
sequence, takes the thread back to before that message.

Lists a thread's sources, after copying the file at `add` among them; a client
fills in its open thread.
Lists the background jobs of a thread; a client fills in its open thread.

through_sequence.description: The newest message the summary covers.

Connector.description: An MCP server a plugin brings.

oneOf.description: The plugin is not here or not on.
The plugin is on and its server is among the connectors.
A connector the user configured has the name; it is used, never replaced.

installed.description: The files are the copy installed here, edits included, not the package's.

package_sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the package, as the list names it or as it was installed.

ContextItemDetail.description: One item's share and how often it is used, so clients can show both.

uses_in_chat.description: Uses in the reported thread; zero when no thread was given.

ContextPolicy.description:
A model's input budget. Auto is the model's own window as its provider reports it,
and [`UNKNOWN_WINDOW`] for a model that reports none. Fixed and Manual are set by
hand; a known window stays their ceiling.

ContextPreset.description: Decimal token counts, matching model catalogue context windows.

sources.description:
What each source category contributed, largest first; empty when nothing was
broken down.

total.description: The size of the next request, as the sidebar counts it.

ContextSection.description: A part of the request; its tokens are estimated, the total may be the provider's.

category.description:
Which source category the section's tokens belong to, for `sources`; empty for
sections that only break down what another section already counted.

details.description: Per-item detail, where the section has it (skills, MCP tools); empty otherwise.

items.description: What it is made of, largest first.

ContextSource.description: One source category's share of the request; only categories with tokens are listed.

CoreInfo.description: What a client learns about the core it reached.

Cost.description: A price in millionths of a US dollar and where it came from.

oneOf.description: The provider reported it with the response.
Counted from the price list in the provider's config.

Cover.description: A picture beside the source's list: a `.png` or `.webp` of at most 512 KiB.

oneOf.description: Also yes to the same folder or program until the core stops.

old.description: Line numbers in the old and the new file; `None` on the side the line is not in.

Effort.description: Reasoning effort. Off is explicit; the provider default omits `reasoning_effort`.

EpisodeKind.description: What an episode the core wrote down is about.

oneOf.description: An error that came back ended with a call that passed.
A goal's verification passed.
The thread's task ended; sending to it opens it again.

What a terminal printed, as raw bytes in the order they came; sent only to the
client that opened it.

The terminal's shell ended, by itself or because the terminal was closed. `code`
is its exit code, or none when a signal ended it.
The view of a plugin's part this client opened, replacing the one before.
A new picture for a `screen` widget of an open part, as JPEG.

The repository of a saved project was changed through the core: open views of
it read it again. Given to clients that may read projects.

A project's repository status changed: its pull requests or their checks, or
the work tree. Given to clients that may read projects.
A plugin's short note, or why its interface stopped.

FileChange.description: One file one tool call changed.

diff.description: A unified diff, when the text before was known and the file is no secret.

diff_cut.description: The diff was cut to its cap; the text ends with a note saying so.

hash_after.description: SHA-256 of the contents after, in hex, when the file was small enough to read.

path.description: Relative to the project folder, with `/` between parts.

size_before.description: `None` for a file that did not exist before (created) or after (deleted).

turn.description: The turn's number in its thread, from 1.

turn_id.description: The turn the call ran in; `None` when it ran outside one.

FileDiff.description: One changed file as a reader of a diff sees it.

binary.description: Contents that are not text, or too large to show: no hunks.

FileEntry.description: One entry of a project folder; hidden and ignored files are left out.

change.description: For a folder, set when anything inside it changed.

path.description: Relative to the project folder, with `/` between parts.

FilePreview.description:
The answer to `StoreRequest::File`: plain text, its control and bidi characters
escaped, at most `PREVIEW_BYTES` of it.

truncated.description: The file is longer than what `text` holds.

text.description:
UTF-8 text a client may ask for with `StoreRequest::File`; anything else, such as
a plugin's program, is shown by its size only.

FileStamp.description:
What a file was on disk at one moment. A client sends back the stamp it read with, so
a file that something else changed meanwhile is not written over.

FileText.description: A text file as the editor opens it.

oneOf.description: Cut by the output token limit.

Found.description: A message found by searching the text of every chat.

sequence.description: The message's place in its chat.

snippet.description: The words around the match, on one line.

GitInfo.description: What a project's repository looks like now; `None` fields outside a repository.

ahead_behind.description: Commits ahead of and behind the upstream, when there is one.

changes.description: Paths relative to the project folder.

stat.description: Lines added and removed in all changes against the last commit.

web.description: The repository's page, from the `origin` remote: https, no credentials.

GitOutcome.description:
What a change of the repository left: git's own words, and the files a merge or a
pull left in conflict.

message.description: Plain and capped; empty when git said nothing.

GitRequest.description:
What to do in a saved project's repository. Paths are relative to the project folder;
branch names are letters, digits and `-_./`. Nothing here forces, amends or prunes.

oneOf.description:
A new branch from `base`, or from the current commit. With `switch` the work tree
moves to it, its changes carried along; git refuses when they would be lost.
Commits what is staged; never amends.

Destructive: the file's uncommitted changes, or the untracked file itself, are
gone. A client asks the user first.
Merges `branch` into the current one; conflicts are reported, not resolved.

A worktree for `branch` beside the repository, in `<repository>-worktrees/`; the
branch is made from `base` (or the current commit) when it does not exist.
Refused while the worktree has uncommitted or untracked files.
Fast-forward only.

The current branch to its upstream, or to `origin` as its new upstream; never
forced. A client asks the user first.
Open pull requests, through the GitHub CLI.
A pull request from the current branch, which must be pushed first.

GoalCriterion.description:
All criteria are mandatory. A command proves exactly the approved check's exit;
a semantic claim always needs a human's review of the saved result.

result_id.description: tool:<saved result message ID> or job:<saved job ID>.

header.description: The `@@ -a,b +c,d @@` line, with the function git names after it.

InstallProgress.description:
Download byte counts stay available through verification and installation.
A missing or zero content length does not give a useful percentage.

JobInfo.description: A job as a client lists it.

status.description:
In words: running, completed, failed, cancelled, timed_out, interrupted, or running
in, or unknown because of, another runtime.

stoppable.description: This runtime owns its process, so it can be stopped from here.

oneOf.description: A set of skills.

Listing.description: One thing a source offers, or a plugin found here.

author.description:
Who made it, one plain line; empty when the list gives none. For a Community
listing it is the mirror's claim, not checked by anyone.

categories.description: One to three of `CATEGORIES`; empty when the list gives none.

category.description: Lower case, `a-z0-9-`; empty when the list gives none.

clash.description:
Another source offers the same name; a client warns, since a mirror may copy a
name to pass for another source's plugin.

connectors.description: For a plugin: the MCP servers it brings.

cover.description: A picture of it, fetched with `StoreRequest::Cover`.

installed.description: The version here, when this source installed it.

license.description: An SPDX expression; empty when the list gives none.

origin.description:
An `https` address of where it comes from: the list's `source`, a name `source`
already has.

permissions.description:
What it may do, one line each, as the user is asked before it is installed: first
one line per `programs`, then one per `connectors`, then what else it may reach.

programs.description:
For a plugin: the command lines of its own programs, run on this computer while it
is on.

repo_stars.description:
GitHub stars of the repository it comes from, only for a mirror the user added;
never for an official or a verified listing, whose count was not the item's own.

screenshots.description:
Pictures of it at work, in order; each fetched with `StoreRequest::Screenshot`
by its place here.

skills.description: For a pack: the skills it holds.

source.description: The source's name; with `name`, what the listing is.

tier.description: How far it is trusted, from the key that signed its list.

unfit.description: Why it cannot be installed on this machine, when it cannot.

update.description: The source's newer version, when this source installed an older one.

upstream.description:
For a skill or pack fetched from its author's repository instead of a package:
`github.com/owner/name at abc1234`.

LocalState.description: Where a model is on this machine.

oneOf.description: What it does now, in a few words.
Installed, and not running.
Why the last install or start did not work.

LogEntry.description: One line of a thread's event log, written by the core from what it stored.

LogKind.description: How a log line ended, which picks its glyph.

McpInfo.description: A server as the settings show it: what the config says and how it stands.

icon.description: Its picture, a file the core found in the config's `icons` folder.

target.description: The command line or the URL.

tools.description: The tools of a ready server, by the name the model calls; empty otherwise.

McpState.description: How a server stands, for clients to show.

oneOf.description: Switched off in the config.
The names of its tools, as the server gave them.

name.description: `server__tool`, the name its switch goes by.

Memory.description:
The memory of the user: whether the agent keeps it, and its size. Every request
carries it, so it is kept small.

artifacts.description: Image cards for clients. Never included in model context or URL detection.

content_tokens.description: Estimated sizes in model tokens; see `estimate_tokens`.

from_job_id.description: A process completion, distinct from user input and system instructions.

from_thread_id.description: For a user message another agent sent: the thread it came from.

reasoning.description: Model thinking; only assistant messages carry it, and only when it was recorded.

tool_call_id.description: Set exactly on tool messages: the call they answer.

summary.description: The first sentence of its prompt.

context_window.description: Maximum input tokens, when the provider's catalogue reports it.

max_output.description: Maximum output tokens of one call, when the catalogue reports it.

ModelEvent.description: One increment of a streamed model response.

oneOf.description: Model thinking: shown to the user and never sent back as context.
A new tool call; its arguments follow as `ToolArguments` with the same index.
A piece of the JSON arguments of the call with this index.

NodeText.description: A skill's or an agent's file as a client edits it.

metadata.description:
The front matter fields with plain values, by name, such as `description` and
`license`.

text.description: The whole file, front matter included.

oneOf.description: A tab of the dock at the right of the work.
A tab of the dock under the work.
A window over the page.

Order.description: The order of the list; the core sorts, so every client shows the same.

oneOf.description: Official, Verified, Community, Local, then by name.
Newest `created` first.
Latest `updated` first.

OutputFile.description: A file the agents made or keep: under the workspace, the pictures folder or a project.

OutputKind.description: What kind of file an output is, as the artifacts page groups them.

OutputPreview.description: How to preview an output image without opening the original.

enabled.description: The skill's own switch, whatever the pack's.

name.description: The skill's full name, such as `engineering/spike`.

Part.description: One part of a plugin, as the core found it in the plugin's manifest.

clients.description: The clients that can draw it; all when empty.

icon.description: The icon as SVG text, checked by the core: small and with nothing it loads.

Picks.description:
Indices into `StoreList::listings`, at most `PICKS` each, best first; a listing
without the date sorted on is left out. Nothing is picked by stars: a mirror writes
its own count, so a shelf of them would rank whoever wrote the biggest number.

compacted.description:
A compaction summed the message up: it is still in the history, no longer in what
the model is sent.

excerpt.description: The start of the message as one line of plain text, cut by the core.

oneOf.description: An icon in the header's tools.
An icon in the rail of places.
An icon beside the message box.
A page under Settings.

PlanCounts.description: How many tasks of a plan are in each status.

PlanPage.description: One page of a plan, for the strip: every task not done, then done ones, newest first.

counts.description: The whole plan's tasks by status, on this page or not.

next.description: The `done_before` of the next page; `None` when no done task is left.

PlanWindow.description: One usage window of a subscription: how long it is and how much of it is used.

minutes.description: How long the window is, in minutes; none when the provider did not say.

resets_in.description: Seconds until it is empty again, counted when the status was made.

clients.description: The clients that can draw its parts; all when empty.

duskcode_version.description: The Dusk Code version it was written for.

missing_settings.description: Settings it asks for that the config does not give.

parts.description: What it brings, such as `mcp` or `hooks`.

permissions.description: What it may do, one line each, as the user allows it by switching it on.

platforms.description: The systems it runs on; all when empty.

problem.description: Why it cannot load, when it cannot.

secrets.description: Its secret settings and whether each is set for this session.

oneOf.description:
Starts the plugin's interface when it is not running; its view follows as
`Event::PluginView`.
Recheck an installed phone dependency and reopen the panel in the new sandbox.

url.description: The list's address the probe read, after a repository's was turned into it.

Problem.description: A node that could not be read, or a link to a node that is not there.

ProcessUsage.description: The running process as `ps` sees it; `None` where `ps` is missing.

cpu_percent.description: Of one core, averaged over the process lifetime on macOS and recently on Linux.

Profile.description: Who the user is, and the files that go with `@me`.

send.description: Whether `@me` attaches it; an unmarked file stays listed for later.

dir.description: Absolute and resolved, with no symbolic links.

ProjectRequest.description:
Projects, and the git state and files of one. Git and files are read only inside
a saved project's folder.

oneOf.description: Saves a new project, or changes the one with `id`; answers with the project.

The changes against the last commit, file by file with their hunks; one file
when `path` is given. Untracked files show as all added.
Refused while the work tree has changes, so nothing is lost.

Changes the repository or reads its pull requests. Answered beside the loop,
since a push or the GitHub CLI may take a while; a change is followed by
`Event::GitChanged`.

The work tree's changes and the pull requests of the repository, answered beside
the loop. The asking client then watches the project, in place of the one it
watched before: while it stays attached the core reads it again, often while
checks run and seldom otherwise, and sends `Event::RepositoryStatus` on a change.

One pull request of the project's own GitHub repository, for a card where a chat
links it; answered beside the loop from what the core knows or read lately, and
read from GitHub at most once at a time and every few minutes per pull request.

The pull requests of each saved project's current branch, from what the core
last read; a project not read yet is read in the background.
The entries of `path`, a folder relative to the project's, `""` for its top.
The files under the workspace and the pictures folder, newest first.
The names of the project's environment variables. Values are never sent back.
Sets one variable for the project's commands; answers with the names.
Removes one; answers with the names left.

A text file for a preview, read only under the workspace, the pictures folder or
a saved project, and only up to `MAX_PREVIEW_BYTES`.

A text file for the editor, read where `ReadOutput` reads and up to
`MAX_EDIT_BYTES`; answers with the text and the file's stamp.

Writes the whole file, only where `ReadFile` reads; a new file is made when its
folder is there. `seen` is the stamp the client read with: the write is refused
when the file on disk no longer has it. Answers with the new stamp.
Removes a file under the workspace or the pictures folder, never a project's.
Every scheduled task, soonest first.

Saves a new scheduled task, or changes the one with the draft's id; answers with
every scheduled task.

Runs it now, in a new chat, without changing when it runs next; answers with
the chat's id.

ProviderErrorKind.description:
What went wrong with a provider call, coarse enough for a client to draw and for the
retry loop to decide on.

oneOf.description:
No response at all: the name did not resolve, the connection or TLS failed, or it
was reset before the provider answered.
Nothing arrived within the idle or model timeout.
The provider asked to slow down (HTTP 429).
The provider is busy or failing (HTTP 5xx, 529, an "overloaded" stream error).
The key or sign-in was not accepted (HTTP 401, 403).
The account or plan has nothing left to spend (HTTP 402, a spent plan).
The provider refused the request itself: bad input, no such model, unsupported.
The provider said the context is too large.
The answer broke off after it began.

ProviderFailure.description: A model call that failed for good: why, and how many times it was sent.

ProviderHealth.description:
How a configured provider's calls went, as the turns that used it since the core
started found. Every field holds until the provider turns healthy or failing or fails
for another reason, so the status is not sent again on every call.

oneOf.description: OpenAI itself: Chat Completions with `max_completion_tokens`.
OpenAI on a ChatGPT plan: the Responses API, signed in to in the browser.
The Anthropic Messages API.
The Google AI Gemini API.

ProviderStatus.description: A configured provider as a check found it: its models, or why it did not answer.

balance.description: What is left on the account; none when the provider does not tell it.

enabled.description: Off: the provider is kept with its key but not asked, so `models` is empty.

failure.description: Why `models` failed, when the core can tell; the text there says it in full.

limits.description: The rate limits its last answer reported; none when it reported nothing.

ProviderTarget.description: Which provider a check asks: one typed in a form and not saved yet, or a saved one.

ProviderWaitKind.description:
A provider failure a turn may wait out because it passes by itself: the provider is
limited, spent or out of reach for now, not refusing this request. Named on the wire
as the `ProviderErrorKind` it stands for.

PullRequest.description: Text fields are plain and capped by the core.

checks.description: All checks together; `None` when there are none.

url.description: The page on GitHub, https only.

PullState.description: Where a pull request stands on GitHub.

PullStatus.description: One pull request as the repository status shows it; text plain and capped.

author.description: The author's login; empty when GitHub gave none.

files.description: How many files it changes; `None` when not known.

url.description: The page on GitHub, https only; empty when GitHub gave none that is safe.

PullSummary.description: The pull requests of a project's current branch, for an icon beside its chats.

checks.description: The worst checks state of them all; `None` when none has checks.

Question.description:
A question as the client shows it. The client always adds a field for the user's
own answer below the options.

multiple.description: Several options may be chosen; otherwise exactly one, or the user's own answer.

RateLimit.description: One limit: how much the account may use in the provider's period, and what is left.

resets_in.description:
Seconds until it is full again, counted when the status was made; none when it
is full or the provider did not say.

RateLimits.description: The rate limits of a provider account, as its last answer reported them.

plan.description:
A subscription's usage windows, such as ChatGPT's five hours and week, by the
share used; empty for a provider that counts requests and tokens.

Refusal.description: Why the core will not go on with a client.

Repeat.description: When a schedule runs. Days are a bit set, bit 0 for Monday to bit 6 for Sunday.

oneOf.description: One run, at a moment in Unix milliseconds.
Every so many minutes, counted from the last run.
Monday to Friday.
Saturday and Sunday.
One day a week, 0 for Monday.
The chosen days.

RepeatRung.description: How far the core went when the model repeated itself within a turn.

oneOf.description: The same call with the same result again: the model is told to change course.

The same error again, through calls that differ: the model is told to stop
varying the call and check its assumption.

The same error yet again: the next step runs at the effort set and the model is
asked for a different plan.
The turn ends as failed, with the error and the attempts.

RepoStars.description:
The star count of a GitHub repository, as the publisher of a list counted it when
signing: the repository's, not a rating of the listing, so it is shown with `repo`.

RepositoryStatus.description:
A project's repository at a glance: the work tree's changes and the pull requests
that matter to it. The core keeps it fresh while a client shows it and sends
`Event::RepositoryStatus` when it changes.

branch.description: `None` on a detached head or outside a repository.

github.description: `owner/repo` of `origin` when it is on github.com; `None` otherwise.

pulls.description: The current branch's pull requests first, then the other open ones; capped.

repository.description: The name of the repository's top folder; empty outside a repository.

stat.description: Lines added and removed in the work tree against the last commit.

unavailable.description:
Why there are no pull requests to show: GitHub CLI missing or signed out, not a
GitHub remote, or GitHub not answering. Plain, for a quiet note; `None` when read.

oneOf.description: A slash command that does not run in a thread.
Recordings in, speech out.
The user's own shell in the window; the agents never see it.
The parts plugins add to the window.
The plugin store; it goes to the network, so it is answered beside the loop.
Installs release `tag`; progress shows in the status until it is done.
Closes every thread and stops the core; the last request a client sends.

Request2.description: What a tool asks to do.

oneOf.description: A path outside the working directory and the workspace.
A shell command line.

Seeing the screen and independent accessibility activation. This never grants
control of the user's system pointer.

Moving and clicking/scrolling with the shared system pointer. This needs its
own session grant, separate from screen access and independent activation.
Window metadata, capture or activation. None is a request to end confinement.

Typing or pressing keys, which can do anything a shell can: asked every time,
with what it sends.
Messages of any chat that contain the searched text.
A page of a root thread's plan.
The team running a root thread's plan, or none before one ran.
How a thread's work stands.
A page of a thread's event log, newest first.
A thread's pins, oldest message first.
Names, sorted: a project's environment variables.
The pinned plan, or none before one was written.
What a check of a provider found.
A PNG or JPEG of a thread's sources.
A sound or picture card the core made.
A thread's own approval mode, or none when it uses the default in settings.
What a change of a repository left.
`None` when the repository has no such pull request or GitHub cannot be asked.
A thread's change ledger, newest first.
A file read for the editor.
What a file is on disk after a write.
The files of a store listing.
One text file of a store listing.
What a repository's list holds, read without saving it.
The repositories the user added, with their state.

A store picture (a cover or a screenshot), checked against its list: its bytes in
base64, and their type.
The request failed; the text says why in full.

Runs.description: What an MCP server is: a program on this computer, or an address on the network.

oneOf.description: The command line, `./` being the plugin's folder.
An `https` address the core sends the agent's requests to.

last_thread_id.description: The chat its last run started.

model.description: `provider/model` the task runs with; `None` takes the chosen one.

next_run_at.description: Unix milliseconds; `None` once it will not run again.

ScheduleDraft.description: What a client sends to make or change a schedule; the core works out when it runs.

ScreenshotRef.description: One screenshot of a listing; its bytes come with `StoreRequest::Screenshot`.

caption.description: Plain text of at most 120 characters, without control characters.

editable.description: The user sets and clears it here; a provider's key goes with the provider.

keychain.description:
The system keychain holds the secrets; without one, provider keys stay in the
private config file and the other secrets cannot be kept.

problem.description: Why the keychain could not be read, such as a lock the user has not opened.

arbiter_default_prompt.description: The built-in review prompt, for an editor to show and reset to.

logging.description: Log files and traces; off writes and sends nothing.

max_attempts.description: Tries of one model call that wrote nothing, the first included.

mode.description: The chat's mode, whose switches `tools` shows.

model_timeout_seconds.description: Seconds a model call may stay silent before it is given up on.

modes.description: Every mode, in the order Tab walks them.

notifications.description: Whether clients notify at all; the bell is the TUI's notification.

sandbox.description: Commands can run confined on this machine.

sound_notifications.description: Whether notifications ring the terminal bell; off stays silent.

tools.description: Every tool by kind and then by name.

version_control.description: Version control settings, shown as their own section.

oneOf.description: Answers with the input limit it gives.
Answers with the minutes saved, after the config's bounds.
Answers with the seconds saved, after the config's bounds.
Answers with the tries saved, after the config's bounds.
Answers with the characters saved, after the config's bounds.
The version control branch prefix; empty adds none.
How auto mode's arbiter judges; empty fields go back to the defaults.
Answers with the mode switched to.
Switches to the mode of this name.
Saves a provider; a model is chosen with `/model`.

Starts a sign-in with a ChatGPT account. Answers with the page to open in the
browser; the status tells how it ends.

Asks a provider for its models and balance, to see whether it answers; nothing is
saved. Answers with `Response::Provider`.

Rebuilds a saved provider's connection, with a new key when one is given, and checks
it. Answers with `Response::Provider`.
Forgets a provider. Refused while its model is the chosen one.

Switches a saved provider on or off; its key stays. Off is refused while its model
is the chosen one.
Forgets every provider and the chosen model.
Keeps a secret in the system keychain; only the names the core knows are taken.
Saves the speech servers; their keys go through `SetSecret`.
Kept in memory for this run only, never in the config file.

problem.description: Why the skill cannot be used as it is; it can still be opened and fixed.

source.description: The company or project it comes from, as its front matter says.

SkillPack.description:
Skills as they came, switched on or off together: the built-in skills as the pack
`duskcode`, and every folder under `skills/` that holds skills, such as a pack from
the store or a plugin's skills. A skill of the user's own at the top is in none.

enabled.description: The pack's own switch; off hides every skill in it.

title.description: From its `pack.yml`; empty when it has none.

error.description: A short reason, without addresses; the core logs the rest.

SourceRow.description: A repository the user added, as `StoreRequest::Sources` read it.

error.description: Why its list was refused; none when it was read.

fingerprint.description: The first 16 hex digits of the SHA-256 of its key.

tier.description: Community, or Verified when the official list vouches for it.

oneOf.description: Speech into text: the microphone.
Text into speech: reading aloud.

Status.description:
Everything a client shows that changes without being asked: sent again whole
whenever any of it changes.

artifacts_dir.description: Where pictures of messages and tool results are kept.

available_update.description: The newer release found on the update channel.

chatgpt.description: How the sign-in with ChatGPT stands.

chatgpt_model.description: The selected model uses a ChatGPT plan connection.

discovering_model.description: The core is still looking for a model over the network.

install.description: How far an update install got, while one runs or once it is done.

limits.description: The rate limits of the current model's account, when its provider reports them.

model.description: The model threads talk to, as `provider/model`.

plugin_parts.description: The parts switched-on plugins add to the window.

provider_health.description:
How the calls to each configured provider went, by name; a provider not asked
since the core started is missing.

updated_builtin.description: Shipped files this start brought to the build's version.

workspace_dir.description: Where a chat without a project works: the root of the workspace folders.

failed.description: The sources that could not be read; the others are listed all the same.

picks.description: The listings a client shows on its shelves, sorted by the core.

oneOf.description:
What the sources offer; answered with `Response::Store`. Only `category`'s, when
it is given, and only of `kinds`, all of them when it is empty: each page asks for
its own, so the core decides what a page lists.

Installs or updates `name` at `version` from `source` and switches it on.
`agreed` is the listing's `permissions` the user was shown; a listing that
changed since is refused.
`tier` is the one the user was shown; the install is refused when the source
earns another one now.
Removes a plugin installed from the store.

Updates every installed plugin whose update asks for nothing more; answered with
`Response::StoreUpdates`.

The cover of `name` from `source`, as the last list read showed it; answered with
`Response::Media`.

The screenshot at `index` of `name`'s `screenshots`, as the last list read showed
them; answered with `Response::Media`.

The files of `name` from `source`: the copy installed here, or else the package
the last list read named, fetched and checked; answered with
`Response::StoreContents`. Nothing of it is installed, run or read by the model.

One text file of the last `Contents` of `name`, by its `path` there; answered with
`Response::StoreFile`.

Reads the signed list at `url` with the Ed25519 `key` (base64) without saving
anything; answered with `Response::StoreProbe`. `url` is a list's `https` address
or a GitHub repository's, whose list is then on its GitHub Pages site.

The repositories the user added, each read now; answered with
`Response::StoreSources`.

Probes `url` with `key` again and, when it passes, saves it as a repository under a
name the core gives it. Its items are Community.
Forgets a repository the user added; what it installed stays.

Switch.description: What a switch in the settings turns on or off.

oneOf.description: A skill pack, by `SkillPack::name`; off hides all its skills.
On sets the policy, off goes back to asking.
Whether clients notify at all.
Whether notifications ring the terminal bell.

SystemReport.description: What the application costs the machine right now.

children.description:
The processes it started and theirs: MCP servers, plugin programs, commands,
terminals; none while there are none or where `ps` is missing.

database_bytes.description: The database file, its write-ahead log and shared memory.

process.description: The app's own process: the window and the core inside it.

Task.description:
A task. Every field after `items` came with the plan graph and has a default, so a
task written before it still reads; such a task's status follows its `done`.

finished_at.description: Set exactly when it is done.

TaskOwner.description: The member thread that holds a task.

TaskStatus.description: Where a task is. Only the core moves a task from one to another.

oneOf.description: Given to a member whose turn has not started.
Handed in; its gate or the lead decides.
Final.

thread_id.description: The root thread, which leads it.

TeamBudget.description:
How much a team may spend unasked. Built and read only through `new`, so a budget
that exists is above zero and within the largest ceilings.

oneOf.description: Every task is done.
Nothing could start, and the lead changed nothing.
The lead or the user stopped it.
The lead reached the cap of agent messages.

TeamMember.description: A thread that holds a task of the plan.

role.description: Its agent definition; `None` is the general agent.

TeamUsed.description:
What a team has used of its budget, counted by the core; it may pass the budget by
the steps already under way.

TerminalRequest.description:
A terminal belongs to the client that opened it: its output comes as events to that
client only, and no other client can name it.

oneOf.description:
Starts the user's shell in `cwd`, a folder inside a saved project or the
workspace; answers with the terminal's id as text.
Keys and pasted text, as the bytes the shell reads.
Ends the shell; `TerminalClosed` follows once it is gone.

Then.description: What a client wants once it has proved itself.

oneOf.description: Stop the core for everyone; only with the key.
Ask the owner's user to restart the core for a newer app; only with the key.

active_at.description: When the newest message or local unsent input was stored, or `created_at`.

name.description: What an agent's thread goes by, such as `Fable-3a`.

owner.description:
The id of the token that started the chat; `None` for the local clients' chats. It is
the token id for now; Phase 3 maps it to the name before any non-full scope sees
other chats.

parent_thread_id.description: For a subagent's thread: the thread that asked it, and the agent's name.

project.description: The folder a chat was started in; `None` for one older than this record.

source.description: Who started the thread, such as `cli`.

temporary.description: It is kept in memory only and is gone when the core stops.

oneOf.description: The active model changed or was discovered after the thread opened.

input_limit.description: The largest request to it: its window or the size set under models.

oneOf.description: Saved locally, outside the model queue, until the client explicitly resends it.

No model is chosen, so a message waits as local unsent until one is. A provider
that fails a turn says so in `TurnFailed`.
A client's request joined the persisted model history, including explicit resends.

The thread is in the middle of `turn`; a client that joined after it began sets
its chat to working. Unlike a replayed `TurnStarted` it opens no fold boundary:
what the client read from history belongs to the same turn.

The running turn waits, as `turn.waiting` says, for the user or for the provider;
it is still the running turn. The next `TurnRunning` of it ends the wait.

A model call failed in a way that may pass; the next attempt follows after a pause.
A client keeps one row for it that each of these replaces; the first `Model` event
of the call is the sign it answered (see `transcript::retry_row`).

max_attempts.description:
None when the call is tried until a time budget runs out instead, as for a
provider that cannot be reached or does not answer in time.

wait_ms.description: The pause before the next attempt.

oneOf.description: Everything the model streams: reasoning, text, tool calls, usage.

The turn ended on an error: the one row that says why. It comes right before that
turn's `TurnFinished`, and again when a chat whose newest turn failed is opened.

The model repeated itself and the core stepped in: the result of the call just
finished carries a note, and at `RepeatRung::Stop` the turn ends. `count` is how
many times the same call, or the same error, came back in this turn.

A model call of the running turn ended: the turn's totals so far, as `Turn` keeps
them, so a client shows them without counting.

The thread got a name: the start of its first message at once, then one the model
gives after the first turn.
The model reached its output cap in one call; the turn ends with what it wrote.
The model refused pictures; they stay files it is told the path of.

The model's answer broke off, such as on a dropped connection; the turn ends with
what it wrote.
The model is summarizing the context; its text streams as `Model` events.
The context stays as it was.

Old tool results were put away: from this request on, each is sent as a one-line
stub that says how to read it back, and the whole text stays stored. Clients
show nothing for it; evals count it.

saved_tokens.description: Estimated tokens each later request carries less.

oneOf.description:
The result of the call just finished is sent shaped: a command's output with
passes, progress and repeats left out and a note on how to read it whole, which
stays stored. Clients show nothing for it; evals count it.

saved_tokens.description: Estimated tokens each later request carries less.

oneOf.description:
The core wrote down what ended a problem in this saved project
(`limits.episodes`). Clients show nothing for it; evals count it.

The thread's token counts, when it starts and after each turn and compaction. `limit` is the largest request: the
configured input limit or the model window, whichever is smaller.

The output generation rate of this thread's agent, over a short rolling window:
about once a second while it generates, and once when a model call ends. A
subagent's rate reaches the client wrapped in `Subagent`, whose `thread_id` says
which agent it is.

tokens_per_sec.description: Generated tokens per second over `window_ms`, counted as context sizes are.

window_ms.description: How wide the window the average covers is, in milliseconds.

oneOf.description:
The context is past the input limit, so the queued turn was not started or the
running one ended; the client should switch model or compact.

The tool call `call_id` gave `task` to `agent`, which works in thread `thread_id`
on `model` (`provider/model`) and reasons at `effort`; `None` is the provider's
default.

model.description: None when no model is chosen, and in events of older cores.

oneOf.description: An event of a subagent's thread. A subagent's own subagents come wrapped once more.

An agent below this chat, a subagent or a team member, is at work (true), or the
last of them ended (false). The chat counts as working while they are, whatever its
own turn does.
The thread's task board changed: every task with its steps.
One task of the plan this thread leads changed; `Tasks` stays for the board.

The team running this thread's plan changed its status, members or budget; at
most one a second.
An agent's phase changed, by its own `agent_state` call or the runtime's.
The agent asks the user to choose; the answer comes as the user's next message.
A tool waits for the user's yes; the client answers through the runtime.
The arbiter answered a request of this thread in the user's place.
The request is answered or its call is gone; the client stops showing it.
Another agent wrote to this thread; the message has joined it.
A background process result joined this thread at a safe execution boundary.

The standing goal changed, or the thread opened with one; `note` says what
happened in a line.

started.description: The message queued to start work on it, for a client to show as sent.

oneOf.description:
/undo took the thread back; `text` is the message it went back to, for the
client to offer again.

The thread's pins changed, by a pin, an unpin or an /undo that took a pinned
message: all of them, oldest message first.
/fork wrote its summary; a client opens a new thread that starts from it.
Nothing is running and nothing will start until the next message.

The thread stopped on an error it could not handle, such as a database failure.
A turn that fails says so in `TurnFailed` instead.

ThreadRequest.description:
Opening, feeding and closing threads. Events of an open thread arrive as
`Event::Thread` until `Event::Ended`.

oneOf.description:
A new chat that is never written to disk: its messages stay in memory and its
files in the system's temporary folder, and all of it goes when the core stops.
A new thread that starts from a /fork summary.

A new thread that holds another's history up to and including one message; from
the latest compaction before it when there is one.
Searches what was said in every chat; at least three characters.

Keeps long pastes and named pictures among the thread's sources, then queues the
message; `now` asks for it before what is queued.

Sends a command the agent runs in the foreground, by its tool call, to the
background: the agent goes on and gets the result when it ends.

Runs a command the user confirmed, in the chat's folder; answers with its output.
`run` is the client's number for it, so `StopRun` can name it.

Kills a command the same client started with `RunCommand`, with everything it
started; its `RunCommand` then answers with an error.
Stops the thread's turn and waits for it to end, so it can be opened again.
Erases the chat, its agents' threads and its files folder for good.

Answers a tool's request for a yes; `false` when it no longer waits or was not
asked in this chat or an agent thread below it.
The thread's own approval mode; `None` goes back to the default in settings.
Answers with the thread's own approval mode, or none when it uses the default.

Pins or unpins one of the thread's messages, at most `MAX_PINS`; answers with
`Response::Pins` and tells the thread's clients `ThreadEvent::Pins`.
Answers with `Response::Pins`: the thread's pins, oldest message first.

all.description: Every message and summary the thread ever had.

context.description:
The best known size of the current context: what the provider counted for the
last call plus estimates of what came after it. Before any call, `current.total()`.

cost_micro_usd.description: The summed cost of the calls whose cost is known.

current.description:
What the model receives now: the system messages, the newest summary and the
messages after it.

spent.description:
Sums of what the provider reported over every model call of the thread and of the
subagents it asked.

unpriced_calls.description: Calls with no known cost: the provider did not report it and no price was set.

Tier.description: Trust, highest first; the list is sorted in this order.

oneOf.description: Signed by the key built into duskcode, and made by duskcode's maintainers.

Signed by the key built into duskcode for somebody else's work, or from a mirror
the official list names with the same address and key.
From a mirror the user added.
Found in the plugins folder, not installed by any source: no key vouches for it.

TokenCounts.description: Estimated tokens by who wrote them.

reasoning.description: The agent's thinking; never sent back, so it is always 0 in the current context.

summary.description: Compaction summaries, which stand in for the older messages.

system.description: The mode's prompt and other system instructions.

tool_specs.description:
Tool definitions, sent with every request but never stored, so the agent counts
them into the current context only.

id.description: Provider-assigned; a tool result refers back to it.

description.description: What the model is told the tool does.

ToolKind.description: What a tool works on, for clients to group tools by; in the order they are shown.

oneOf.description: The thread itself: its history, tasks and skills.
The screen: screenshots, mouse and keyboard. Heavy, so off until switched on.

ToolResult.description: What the model gets back from a call.

exit_code.description: Set only by the foreground shell runner, never inferred from output text.

name.description: As the model called it: data, drawn as plain text.

cost_micro_usd.description: The summed cost of the turn's calls whose cost is known.

last_sequence.description: Sequence of the newest user message this turn answers.

steps.description:
The model calls of the turn that answered so far. This and the two below are
counted by the core; absent from older peers, which sent no spend.

tokens.description: Prompt and completion tokens of every model call of the turn.

waiting.description:
Set while the running turn waits; never on a turn that ended. Absent from older
peers, which knew no waits.

TurnFailure.description: Why a turn failed: what the one row at its end shows.

error.description: Safe to show: never a key, a header, a request body or a URL path.

provider.description: Set when the turn failed on a model call.

oneOf.description: Stopped by the user or a restart; a partial answer is kept when there was one.

TurnWait.description: What a running turn waits for. Times are Unix timestamps in milliseconds.

oneOf.description: A restart cut off a call that may have taken effect; the user decides.

The provider cannot serve the turn now; it continues by itself at `wake_at`.
`since` is when the first of the waits in a row began, which bounds them all.

UiEvent.description: What a widget sends back; places on a screen are in its own whole units.

oneOf.description: One phase of a press on a screen, for drags and long presses.
A key pressed while a screen has focus, by name, such as `return`.
Text typed while a screen has focus.
A wheel turned over a screen at `x`, `y`; the finger moves by `dx`, `dy` units.

UndoPoint.description: A user message the thread can go back to.

commits_behind.description: Commits from the running version to a newer `latest`, when GitHub knows both.

latest.description: The newest version on the channel, as its tag.

newer.description: `latest` is newer than the running version.

ready.description:
The release has the archive for this target; right after a tag it may still be
building on GitHub.

skipped.description: Updates left for the user, by name, with why.

Usage.description: Token usage of the whole request, as the provider reports it.

cache_write_tokens.description:
The part of the prompt written to the cache, which some providers bill above
plain input.

cached_prompt_tokens.description: The part of the prompt the provider served from its cache, usually at a discount.

completion_tokens.description: Everything the model wrote, its reasoning included.

cost.description:
What the call cost, when the provider said so or the user's price list has the
model; never guessed.

prompt_tokens.description: Everything the request sent, the cached part included.

VersionControl.description: Version control settings; clients show this section as "Version control".

branch_prefix.description: The prefix for branch names this tool creates, such as `dusk/`; empty adds none.

VoiceEndpoint.description: One server and the model to ask of it. The key is kept apart, in the keychain.

voice.description: The voice of a synthesis server; unused for recognition.

in_use.description: The chat's speech settings point at it.

size.description: What it takes on disk, such as "1.6 GB".

VoiceModels.description: The models, and whether `uv`, which installs them, is on this machine.

oneOf.description: Turns a WAV recording into text; `wav` makes one from samples.
Reads text aloud; answers with the sound as a card of the artifact store.
The speech models of this machine and where each one is.

Installs a model with `uv`, starts it and sets the chat's speech to it. Answers at
once; `Models` shows the progress.
Stops an install that is under way and deletes what it had made.
Stops a model, deletes it and what it downloaded.

VoiceSettings.description: What is set up: recognition and synthesis are independent, and either may be missing.

WaitsOn.description: What a blocked task waits for.

oneOf.description: A task of the plan that failed, by its id.
A message of the team's mailbox that nobody answered yet, by its id.
A task in review that the core held for the lead's decision.

Widget.description: A widget. Ids name the widget in the events it sends back.

oneOf.description: A one-line text field; `Input` comes back when it is submitted.
A list to choose from; a menu when `menu` is set.

A live picture the plugin sends frames for, such as a device's screen. It takes
taps and swipes in its own `width` by `height` units; `phone` draws a phone's
body around it.
Work under way.

WindowAccess.description: Window inventory or one kind of access to a retained window selection.

WorkHistory.description: Compact facts about the current project, kept separately from user memory.

WorkRequest.description:
A thread's background jobs, sources, plan, team and changes. The plan and team
requests name the root thread, which leads the team.

oneOf.description:
A PNG or JPEG of up to `MAX_PICTURE_UPLOAD` bytes, sent by a client that cannot
name a file on this machine, such as a browser; kept among the thread's sources.
Answers with the tag that puts it in a message.

The bytes of the thread's picture source `name`, as its tag names it, for a
client to draw. Answers with `Response::Picture`; a source that is no PNG or
JPEG is refused.

A part of a card a message of the thread, or of an agent thread below it, carries:
`image`, `audio` or `thumb`. Answers with `Response::Picture`, or an error when the
thread has no such card.
The chat's pinned plan, a Markdown text the user and the model both edit.
Rewrites the plan; empty text removes it.

The changes in the chat's own folder against the last commit, as `Diff` of a
project answers; the folder is the one the chat started in.
The files the chat's commands changed in its project.

What the chat's commands changed in its project, file by file with diffs, newest
first, at most `MAX_FILE_CHANGES`.

The plan for the strip: every task not done, then up to `limit` done ones older
than the task `done_before`, newest first; the core holds `limit` to
`PLAN_PAGE_DONE`. Answers with `Response::PlanPage`.
The team running the plan. Answers with `Response::Team`.

How the thread's work stands: its activity, changes and newest log lines. Answers
with `Response::Overview`.

The thread's event log older than `before` (Unix ms), newest first; the core holds
`limit` to `EVENTS_PAGE`. Answers with `Response::Events`.
Passes the `user_confirmation` gate of a task in review.
Ends the running team as stopped.
Sets the running team's budget, within the ceilings of the settings.
